newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower in mixed trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower in mixed trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly lower on Tuesday in mixed and dull trading which traders said reflected a market mired in a mood of uncertainty.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.23 percent, or 0.58 points, to 251.52 on all-share turnover of 90 million shekels against 91 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Jewish holiday of Passover.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.18 percent lower at 261.89.
"The market was mixed and selective as investors wait to see where the economy is going," said Amir Eyal of Epsilon Securities.
"It is not clear what will happen with inflation and if the economy is slowing down. There are many contradicting indicators and we need more information," he said.
Yigal Mizrahi, chief analyst at Nesuah Trading and Investments, said: "Investors are sitting on the fence waiting for further developments on the political and economic front."

Mizrahi said the government, hit recently by a corruption scandal that threatened the ruling coalition of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, is "busy with its problems" and has no time to deal with the economy.
"The fact that the market remained at the same level despite all the uncertainty shows that the trend is still positive," Mizrahi said.
Traders said investors remained indifferent to the Bank of Israel's decision on Thursday to leave its key lending rate unchanged at 13.9 percent in May.
"The market did not expect a rate cut and the central bank's decision had no impact on trading," Eyal said.

Electra Consumer Products fell 0.25 percent to 1,935 agorot. Sahar Securities and Investments maintained its hold recommendation for Electra, saying the air conditioner maker will recover slowly from a weak 1996 fourth quarter.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 2.25 percent to 16,786 agorot on volume of 9.6 million shekels; Israel Discount Bank, which dropped 1.25 percent to 343 agorot on volume of 6.8 million shekels; and Koor Industries which slid 2.75 percent to 28,992 agorot on volume of 5.4 million shekels.
